newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, recovery in doubt.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, recovery in doubt.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower, giving back some of the gains seen earlier this week, and raising doubts about whether the downtrend since early September was over.
"It was very disappointing," Linnco Futures Group Chicago-based analyst Anthony Raia said.

"Precious metals should have continued to rally, aided by the continued stock market weakness, but we saw some trade hedging help push the market back down again from levels that were near chart resistance points," he added.

"The recovery stalled yesterday with December gold failing to get to the $387.50 resistance area, and December silver struggled above $5.000, failing to get near resistance around $5.100, which suggests the outlook remains bearish."
COMEX December gold ended down $1.00 an ounce at $384.90, after finding some support at the intraday lows at $384.50.
In bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted $382.85/383.25, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $383.00 and the New York close Wednesday at $383.60/384.10.
COMEX December silver closed down 7.0 cents at $4.918 an ounce, seeing a session low at $4.890.
Earlier this week the precious metals complex had recovered to two week highs, helped by fund shortcovering and expectations for improved seasonal physical offtake.
But precious metals also received little support Thursday from a third day of losses in U.S. equity markets.

The complex also failed to respond to an unexpectedly sharp drop in U.S. weekly jobless claims, released early Thursday, even though it suggested a tight labor market which could be inflationary, analysts said.

"For the longer term, we still believe a shortage of new supply should lead to a sustainable higher price, but it will take longer for the fundamentals to assert themselves," Smith Barney mining analyst Victor Lazarovici said in a report.

While we believe the gold market supply deficit allows for and requires a considerable degree of official sector selling and producer hedging, the high degree of speculative activity and technically based trading leaves the market susceptible to mood swings," he said.
"Given the current mood, we believe a lower trading range will prevail over the next 12-18 months than we previously forecast."
NYMEX January platinum closed down $1.90 an ounce at $390.00, after first building on Wednesday's gains by pushing up intraday to a four week high at $393.50.
NYMEX December palladium ended down $1.10 an ounce at $119.00.
--Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
